item.title: LOT-108: video sheet "open the link" fallback, no provider before the tap
item.body:
## Issue
Closes #199
Claim: cloud/lot-108
LOT-108

## What and why
LOT-083 already shipped the placeholder, the tap event and `VideoPlayerSheet` (see `docs/lots/LOT-108-video-placeholder.md`). This lot adds what was left:
- "Ouvrir le lien" toolbar button on `VideoPlayerSheet`, on the member's original link (`MessageEmbed.sourceURL`), `http`/`https` with a host only, via the system `openURL` (YouTube app by universal link, else Safari). It also shows when the player URL fails its host check, where the sheet now explains it.
- Tests that nothing of the provider loads before the tap. Spec `docs/lots/LOT-108-video-placeholder.md` (legacy pointer `LinkItem.m:148-158` @ 2440d79, GAP-058).

No change to `TopicHTMLBuilder` or `TopicReaderView` (small footprint next to #463). dev-swift merged in.

## How it was verified
- `VideoPlayerSheetTests`: player URL (https, provider host, no port) and fallback URL (`tel:`/`file:` refused).
- `ReaderWebControllerTests.aVideoPlaceholderRequestsNothingFromTheProviderUntilTapped` (real web view): no `iframe`, serialized page names no provider URL, transport and image policy saw no provider host, web view stays on the reader page, a tap reports `(post, index, token)`.
- SwiftLint clean locally. The app cannot be built in the cloud: CI `App build + tests` is the arbiter. Tests not yet shown failing without the change (no Mac/CI run).
- Adversarial review (Opus), round 1: APPROVE, 3 low findings, all fixed in 2a9d223.

## Checklist (AGENTS.md §9)
- [x] Module boundaries respected
- [x] Tests added
- [x] No secrets; fixtures anonymized
- [x] Docs updated (lot spec); issue to be closed by hand after merge
- [x] Author model: Sonnet 5.5 / Reviewer model: Opus
- [ ] Legacy behaviour change line in `docs/CHANGELOG-LEGACY.md`: not added (no legacy fix; the placeholder change is LOT-083/071's)

## Mac check needed (for `mac/m2-lead`)
- [ ] Placeholder and sheet render: light, dark, Dynamic Type XL, iPhone 18 Pro and iPad.
- [ ] Real playback of a YouTube, a Vimeo and a Streamable video in the sheet.
- [ ] "Ouvrir le lien" with and without the YouTube app installed (what `openURL` does), and with a Streamable `http` link.
- [ ] Sheet for an embed whose player URL is refused (unavailable view + button).
- [ ] `xcodebuild test` on both simulators; confirm the new web test executes.

---

The action requires an explicit tap and accepts only web links. No automatic opening or expanded app privileges were identified. Actual browser or video-app handling was not exercised in this review. **Retained concerns** No architecture-level concerns identified.
Security review details

**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The new exposure is user-initiated external navigation of the selected embed’s original source. The inspected action does not invoke the authenticated forum client, modify account state, or automatically fetch that source before selection. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — The original URL remains member-controlled input. The unchanged detector recognizes supported provider-link forms and retains that original URL separately from the constructed player URL. At the external-navigation sink, fallback validation permits HTTP(S) URLs with a host; it does not apply the player’s provider allowlist, port, or username restrictions. - _inferred_ — The external handoff intentionally leaves the nonpersistent player context. Browser or associated-app storage, authentication, redirects, and subsequent navigation are outside the player controls inspected here; the initial HTTP(S) check is not a guarantee about downstream behavior. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _observed_ — The added web-view tests assert absence of provider requests before a placeholder click and an unchanged reader URL after it. A separate positive control checks that the loopback recorder observes an actual WebKit connection. These are source-level assertions, not verified execution results from this review.

A second test is the positive control: a plain `WKWebView` loading that server must register a connection. Not run in the cloud (no app build); CI will show it.
